- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., >70) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward by 1–2% for first 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment to counteract.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to underestimate late-period (days 25–30) — increase by 0.5–1.5% for final 5 days if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.70” values, model underperforms — apply +1% correction to forecast for next 3–5 days.
